test_title: PYST 6: SSC GD Constable 2022 - English (Held On : 11 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful.

My ________ intention was to have a good time in the excellent _______.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e. **'Sole; weather'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate **option to fill** in the blanks in the sentence is **"sole; weather".**

 
• **"Sole"** as an adjective means "only" or "single". In this context, it implies that the speaker had only one intention or purpose, which was to have a good time. 
 
• **"Weather" **refers to the state of the atmosphere at a place and time as regards heat, dryness, sunshine, wind, rain, etc. 
 
• **In this context**, it refers to the conditions outside that would impact the speaker's good time.

Therefore, the **c****orrect sentence** is: *'My** sole** intention was to have a good time in the excellent **weather.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:

 
 
• **"Soul; weather":** "Soul" refers to the spiritual or immaterial part of a human being or animal, which is not typically used to refer to intentions. So, this choice doesn't make much sense in this context.
 
• **"Soul; whether":** This choice is grammatically incorrect. "Whether" is a conjunction used to introduce alternatives. It does not fit in the second blank.
 
• **"Sole; whether": **As explained before, "whether" doesn't fit in the context of the sentence.
